report.source_text: A 2-day-old Caucasian female patient has been transferred straight from maternity to our hospital. The main concern was reverse peristalsis, together with significant abdominal distention and inability of passing stools with fever. On the same day, an adequate stimulation resulted in defecation, reverse peristalsis stopped, and abdominal distention (circumference) was reduced. Enteral feeding resumed; however, the patient could not pass stools without stimulation.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-day-old female neonate presented with reverse peristalsis, significant abdominal distention, inability to pass stools, and fever. Initial stimulation induced defecation and reduced symptoms. A contrast enema at day 4 showed no transition zone. Full-thickness biopsy specimens from rectum and colon taken during surgical intervention on day 75 underwent histology and immunohistology staining, confirming the diagnosis of total colonic aganglionosis by pathology.
